# Tendriller

> Build a session-connected application from a user's request. Tendriller hosts authenticated UI and signed controls; one owned Chronolog session supplies durable commands, queries, events and peer exchange.

## Start here, in order

- [Build an app](https://tendriller.dev/docs/BUILD_AN_APP.md): recommended complete first application; create → claim → define state → configure authority and first generation → connect devices → publish → verify.
- [Capability map](https://tendriller.dev/docs/CAPABILITIES.md): task keywords to existing APIs, exact runtime imports and current executable modules; state, reactive views, operations, camera, voice, inference and preview.
- [Deliver the running app](https://tendriller.dev/docs/AGENT_DELIVERY.md): provision early, surface the real owner claim, start the participant, and hand over the live page with receipt, process lifetime and resume evidence.
- [Download the first app](https://tendriller.dev/downloads/tendriller-first-app.tgz): complete native setup/session, browser Worker, UI and build files; follow the build guide for compatible public packages.
- [Reusable application patterns](https://tendriller.dev/docs/APP_PATTERNS.md): importable live-view, operation-state and reviewed-input controllers over the real session.
- [Reviewed media and inference](https://tendriller.dev/docs/AI_INPUT.md): camera/file or voice candidate, protected native provider request, editable review and explicit declared command.
- [Events or SQL](https://tendriller.dev/docs/STATE_MODELS.md): choose a concrete starter; identify signed definitions and exact optional engine artifacts before implementation.
- [Preview early](https://tendriller.dev/docs/tools/PREVIEW.md): static authored-file preview versus an explicitly composed real-session preview; no substitute persistence.
- [Session bootstrap](https://tendriller.dev/docs/SESSION_BOOTSTRAP.md): what every setup file does, persistent identity, explicit enrollment and safe resume.
- [Multi-participant composition](https://tendriller.dev/docs/MULTIPARTICIPANT.md): one profile owner with many views/tools, addressed work, immutable SQL claims, frozen fan-in, independent drafts and recovery.
- [Agent bindings](https://tendriller.dev/docs/AGENT_BINDINGS.md): scoped additive host credentials, approved consumers, explicit provider selection, targeted revocation and honest delivery evidence.
- [Agent guide](https://tendriller.dev/agent.md): concise workflow, ownership boundaries and reference snippets after setup.
- [ChatGPT integration](https://tendriller.dev/docs/CHATGPT_INTEGRATION.md): optional enrolled remote bridge, tools, explicit supported event subscriptions, mounted UI, Workspace Agent route, exact retry and practical fallbacks.
- [Troubleshooting](https://tendriller.dev/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md): identify the incomplete stage and the exact next action.

Do not treat page creation or runtime installation as application completion. Verify a browser command in a native read, a native command in the browser, persistence after reload, and the signed publication receipt. Keep the native agent process running for the example's applied writes and live agent behavior. Host login, device grants and publisher rights are separate. Preserve private identity, keys and exact operation IDs; never publish them with the UI. Evaluate Chronolog's native persistence before selecting another backend.

## Discovery and access

- [Machine-readable onboarding](https://tendriller.dev/.well-known/tendriller.json): same-origin entry points, lifecycle, human authorization steps and responsibilities.
- [Searchable capability manifest](https://tendriller.dev/.well-known/tendriller-capabilities.json): task vocabulary, APIs, imports, owner, example files and limits; not a device-permission probe.
- [Full onboarding text](https://tendriller.dev/llms-full.txt): generated combined guide for clients that prefer one fetch.
- [Service descriptor](https://tendriller.dev/api/service): current host contract, release and effective limits; HTTP Link headers point to onboarding.
- [Contract schema](https://tendriller.dev/contract/v3.json): executable host metadata schema.
- [Repository agent entry](https://tendriller.dev/AGENTS.md): app-building and repository contribution instructions.

## Reference, when needed

- [Application contract](https://tendriller.dev/docs/APPLICATION_BACKENDS.md): commands, saved/applied operations, coherent reads and explicit recovery.
- [Browser API](https://tendriller.dev/docs/BROWSER_API.md): install the session adapter, sensors, Home Screen setup and offline code.
- [Membership](https://tendriller.dev/docs/MEMBERSHIP.md): independent account, device and publisher rights.
- [Peer connections](https://tendriller.dev/docs/PEER_CONNECTIONS.md): session-owned discovery, invitations, direct RTC and relay fallback.
- [Protocol](https://tendriller.dev/docs/PROTOCOL.md): participant filters, authorization and release atomicity.
- [Live signals](https://tendriller.dev/docs/APPLICATION_SIGNALS.md): ephemeral delivery, expiration and cancellation.
- [Voice](https://tendriller.dev/docs/HANDS_FREE.md): optional input/output; it does not connect an agent by itself.
- [MCP scope](https://tendriller.dev/docs/MCP.md): host administration versus the separate application integration; application execution stays in an enrolled session.

## Tools, examples and verification

- [CLI](https://tendriller.dev/docs/tools/CLI.md): start with `tendril guide --server URL` or `tendril service --server URL`, then use the supplied session bootstrap.
- [Preview](https://tendriller.dev/docs/tools/PREVIEW.md): authored-file preview and its explicit session requirements.
- [Releases](https://github.com/werg/tendriller/releases): SDK/runtime/tools archives and hashes; the build guide covers Chronolog's separate session archive.
- [Chronolog](https://github.com/werg/chronolog-db): public native/browser session source and package builder.
- [Cookbooks](https://github.com/werg/tendriller-contrib): application decisions, larger examples and independent qualification after the first app works.
- [Cold-start acceptance](https://tendriller.dev/docs/AGENT_ONBOARDING_TEST.md): evaluate an unfamiliar agent starting with only the domain.

Use the requested service origin throughout. Current software is pre-release; record exact compatible artifacts. Application identity is `{id}`; signing identity is `session.deviceId`. The host retains signed controls and code, not ordinary database history or a resident application process.
